children: Neighborhood Intelligence, the company previously known as Bed, Bath and Beyond, said its finance chief will leave the company after calling off its merger with Fathom.
With Brian LaRose departing, Paul Kosturos, managing director of Alvarez & Marsal, will step in as interim chief financial officer.
LaRose stepped in around the time that Neighborhood Intelligence acquired The Container Store earlier this year.
Since the July closing of The Container Store deal, Neighborhood Intelligence has been working with Alvarez & Marsal to streamline its business.

Based on an assessment by the consultant, Neighborhood Intelligence has reconfigured its supply chain team and strategy. The company is in the process of rebalancing its inventory and has started exiting several dozen locations, with those closures expected to be complete by year-end.

The company has also remade its finance team. In August, it appointed Jill Windrum as chief accounting officer and deputy chief financial officer. Emma Haugh has also been added to the finance team as retail chief financial officer.

Earlier on Monday, Neighborhood Intelligence and Fathom terminated their merger after concluding that the current valuations in the proposed deal wouldn't appropriately reflect the fair value of either company.

The companies had announced plans for the deal back in June, before Neighborhood Intelligence bought The Container Store. Neighborhood Intelligence planned to buy the real-estate services platform Fathom for about $53.4 million in equity.

title: Neighborhood Intelligence Names New CFO Amid Restructuring
